heading: More time for
the human side.
intro: Give your customer success team the operational support to stay present. Organize onboarding, account signals, reviews, and follow-up around the relationships you want to build.
storyHeading: Make the next customer conversation easier.
story: Customers experience your team as one relationship, even when the work crosses several systems. A support specialist keeps the record connected: agreed actions, current resources, open questions, and the next accountable owner.
footer: Remote customer success operations support for onboarding, account health, business reviews, adoption, renewals, and customer feedback.
close: Keep your team closer to your customers.
name: customer-success-managers

services.title: Customer onboarding support
services.description: Keep plans, tasks, and approved communication organized.
services.intro: Turn an approved onboarding plan into a visible operating rhythm. A remote specialist can maintain the record, prepare reminders, reconcile task ownership, and surface blocked steps while the account owner leads the relationship.
services.audience: Customer success teams with a defined onboarding plan but inconsistent task updates, reminders, handoffs, or blocker visibility.
inputs: Approved onboarding plan and stage definitions
Named source systems and required record fields
Current owner, dependency, and escalation map
Approved reminder templates and communication rules
work: Prepare onboarding records from approved templates
Maintain task owners, dates, and dependency notes
Coordinate approved reminders and meeting logistics
Reconcile completed steps with source systems
Flag blocked steps to the named account owner
outputs: A current onboarding record
Clear next actions after each touchpoint
Visible blockers with an accountable owner
Consistent handoff notes for the account team
controls: Required fields are complete before a record advances
Dates and status changes trace to the named source
Blocked steps have an owner and documented transfer
A sample of completed journeys is reviewed for record completeness
boundaries: No product, pricing, scope, or delivery promises
No changes to contract or implementation commitments
No independent interpretation of security requirements
workflow: Receive the approved plan and customer stage
Check required fields and source freshness
Prepare the next approved action or reminder
Record the response and update status
Transfer exceptions to the accountable owner
scenarios: A growing implementation queue needs daily record maintenance
Kickoff notes are not consistently transferred into the onboarding plan
Account owners need blockers separated from routine follow up

faqs.question: Does the specialist own the customer relationship?
faqs.answer: No. The account owner retains relationship judgment, commitments, and customer-facing decisions. The specialist maintains the approved operating record and routes exceptions.

faqs.question: Can support change the onboarding plan?
faqs.answer: Only approved updates are recorded. Scope, delivery, security, and product decisions return to the authorized owner.

services.title: Customer health operations
services.description: Prepare consistent views from approved health signals.
services.intro: Give customer leaders a review-ready view of the signals they have already approved. Support can reconcile source dates, assemble portfolio summaries, and route threshold exceptions without inventing a score or deciding account strategy.
services.audience: Customer success leaders who already have approved health indicators but need a repeatable way to reconcile, prepare, and review them.
inputs: Approved indicators and definitions
Named systems, source dates, and refresh cadence
Portfolio review template and threshold rules
Review owner and exception route
work: Compile approved product, support, and engagement indicators
Check source dates and missing inputs
Prepare portfolio and account review summaries
Maintain risk and opportunity follow-up queues
Flag threshold exceptions for owner review
outputs: Health views with visible source dates
Missing-data exceptions separated from true risk
A repeatable portfolio review packet
A clear queue for account-owner decisions
controls: Every signal shows its source date
Missing data is separated from account risk
Definitions remain unchanged during preparation
Threshold exceptions are sampled against source records
boundaries: No independent health-score design
No churn prediction claims or automated account decisions
No commercial or customer communication without approval
workflow: Collect approved indicators from named systems
Validate freshness and required fields
Assemble the agreed view without changing definitions
Mark missing or conflicting inputs
Route the summary to the review owner
scenarios: Weekly portfolio reviews begin with manual source reconciliation
Missing usage or support data is being mistaken for risk
Leadership needs a consistent packet without delegating account strategy

faqs.question: Will support design our health score?
faqs.answer: No. The team supplies approved definitions and thresholds. Support prepares the view and surfaces missing or conflicting evidence.

faqs.question: Does this predict churn?
faqs.answer: No. The scope organizes approved evidence for accountable review and makes no prediction or guaranteed outcome claim.

services.title: Business review preparation
services.description: Organize context and materials for accountable account owners.
services.intro: Reduce meeting preparation time without outsourcing the customer relationship. A specialist can assemble approved outcomes, open actions, adoption context, and logistics so the account owner can focus on the conversation and decisions.
services.audience: Account teams that spend too much meeting time gathering context, checking action logs, and chasing approved inputs.
inputs: Meeting purpose, participants, date, and approved template
Current outcomes, adoption context, and open actions
Decision log and customer-safe language
Named reviewers and packet cutoff
work: Prepare meeting briefs and agenda drafts
Compile approved outcomes and usage context
Maintain action and decision logs
Coordinate invitations and approved follow-up
Route strategic questions to the right owner
outputs: A consistent pre-meeting brief
Current action and decision records
Fewer missing inputs before the review
Prompt follow-through after the meeting
controls: Every material statement traces to an approved source
Open actions show an owner and date
Missing inputs are visible before the review cutoff
Follow up records match approved meeting decisions
boundaries: No presentation of unapproved claims
No negotiation of renewal, price, or scope
No product roadmap or delivery commitments
workflow: Confirm meeting purpose, participants, and template
Collect approved facts from named sources
Identify gaps for owner review
Assemble the packet and logistics
Record approved actions and route follow-up
scenarios: Quarterly reviews rely on last-minute document assembly
Action items are separated across notes and systems
Account owners need a consistent brief while retaining the conversation

faqs.question: Can the specialist present the review?
faqs.answer: The scope prepares materials and logistics. The accountable account owner leads customer decisions, commitments, and the relationship.

faqs.question: Can unverified results be included?
faqs.answer: No. Gaps are flagged for review rather than filled with assumptions or unapproved claims.

services.title: Adoption follow up support
services.description: Coordinate approved education and next steps around product use.
services.intro: Keep approved education and next steps moving after the account owner defines the adoption plan. Support can prepare segmented queues, send approved resources, log responses, and escalate risk signals without giving product advice beyond reviewed materials.
services.audience: Teams with an approved adoption plan whose education, reminders, response capture, and next-step routing are inconsistent.
inputs: Approved audience and follow-up rules
Current education resources and message templates
Consent, status, and contact records
Risk signals and accountable owner route
work: Prepare follow-up queues from approved criteria
Send approved learning resources and reminders
Record customer responses and requested help
Maintain attendance and completion records
Escalate adoption risks or unclear requests
outputs: A visible follow-up queue
Consistent use of current approved resources
Customer responses captured for the owner
Risks separated from routine reminders
controls: Only current approved resources are used
Audience and consent rules are checked before outreach
Responses retain the customer meaning
Questions and risk signals transfer within the agreed window
boundaries: No unapproved advice or custom product commitments
No independent targeting or pressure tactics
No security, legal, or commercial interpretation
workflow: Receive approved audience and outreach rules
Check consent, status, and current resource version
Prepare or send the approved message
Record delivery and response status
Route questions or risk signals to the owner
scenarios: Education follow up is delayed after training or launch
Multiple resource versions are being sent
Customer responses need consistent capture for the account owner

faqs.question: Can support give custom product advice?
faqs.answer: No. Support uses approved materials and transfers questions that require product, security, commercial, or strategic judgment.

faqs.question: Who defines the follow-up audience?
faqs.answer: The accountable team defines the audience and approved rules. The specialist prepares and maintains the resulting queue.

services.title: Knowledge operations
services.intro: Help teams keep customer-facing guidance findable and current. A specialist can manage the inventory, version records, review queue, and publication checklist while subject-matter owners approve every substantive change.
services.audience: Customer success organizations with growing customer-facing guidance, unclear ownership, or inconsistent review and publication records.
inputs: Knowledge inventory and current source records
Named subject-matter owners and reviewers
Version, review, retention, and publication rules
Approved update request with source evidence
work: Maintain the knowledge inventory and ownership record
Track approved versions and review dates
Route update requests to subject-matter owners
Apply approved edits and publication checks
Flag duplicate, stale, or conflicting guidance
outputs: A searchable source of current guidance
Visible owners and review dates
A controlled path from request to publication
Fewer stale or conflicting resources
controls: Every published item has a current owner and review date
Approved source and final version remain traceable
Superseded material is handled under retention rules
Publication checklist completion is sampled
boundaries: No independent policy or product interpretation
No publication without the required approval
No removal of retention or evidence records
workflow: Receive an update request with source evidence
Identify the current approved record and owner
Prepare the requested change for review
Publish only after documented approval
Record version, date, and superseded material
scenarios: Customer guidance exists across several repositories
Update requests lack a visible review owner
Teams need stale or conflicting resources routed for decision

faqs.question: Will support write policy or interpret the product?
faqs.answer: No. Subject-matter owners approve every substantive change. Support manages the inventory, workflow, approved edits, and publication checks.

faqs.question: Can old guidance simply be deleted?
faqs.answer: Only under the approved retention process. Version and evidence records are preserved where required.

services.title: Escalation coordination
services.description: Document context and route issues to the right accountable owner.
services.intro: Create a disciplined record around issues that need accountable judgment. Support can capture the original request, gather approved context, maintain status, and track promised actions while authorized leaders decide severity, response, remedy, and customer commitments.
services.audience: Customer teams that need a complete, current escalation record while authorized leaders decide severity, response, remedy, and commitments.
inputs: Original customer request and source record
Approved account context and timeline sources
Escalation matrix, status fields, and update cadence
Authorized owners for response, remedy, and closure
work: Prepare escalation records from the original request
Gather approved timeline and account context
Maintain owner, status, and next-action fields
Coordinate approved internal updates
Track promised actions and acknowledgements
outputs: A complete escalation record
One visible owner and current next action
A timestamped handoff trail
Fewer status gaps during resolution
controls: The original customer meaning is preserved
Required context and source links are present
Owner acknowledgement and next action are timestamped
Closure requires documented authorized confirmation
boundaries: No independent severity, remedy, or liability decision
No customer promise without authorized approval
No alteration of the original complaint or source record
workflow: Capture the original issue without rewriting its meaning
Check required context and source links
Route by the approved escalation matrix
Record owner acknowledgement and status
Close only with documented owner confirmation
scenarios: Status updates are spread across chat, tickets, and notes
Issues move between teams without a visible owner
Leaders need a reliable timeline before deciding the response

faqs.question: Does the coordinator decide severity or remedy?
faqs.answer: No. Authorized leaders keep those decisions. The coordinator prepares the record, routes it through the approved matrix, and tracks acknowledged actions.

faqs.question: Can the coordinator promise a resolution date?
faqs.answer: Only an explicitly approved commitment may be recorded or communicated. Unapproved promises are outside scope.

services.title: Renewal coordination support
services.description: Prepare timelines, source records, and internal handoffs before the renewal conversation.
services.intro: Prepare timelines, source records, and internal handoffs before the renewal conversation. A focused administrative role maintains the agreed record and prepares useful next actions, with exceptions kept visible for the person who has authority to resolve them.
services.audience: customer success leaders, SaaS operators, and account teams
inputs: The current workflow, source systems, and approved access
Your templates, definitions, and completion criteria
A named review owner, communication cadence, and escalation rules
work: Maintain the approved renewal calendar and account owners
Collect current contract and usage references from authorized systems
Prepare internal reminders and meeting context
Track unanswered questions and agreed next steps
outputs: A review-ready renewal brief
An accountable renewal action queue
Current records for the account owner
controls: Compare each completed item with its approved source.
Check that the status, owner, and next action agree across records.
Keep missing or conflicting information visible until the review owner resolves it.
Review a sample together before expanding the volume or scope.
boundaries: No pricing, concession, contract acceptance, or renewal commitment
Your account team leads the commercial relationship
workflow: Agree on the first queue, the expected output, and who reviews the work.
Walk through representative records together and document ambiguous cases.
Begin with a manageable volume and a regular exception review.
Use corrections and completion checks to refine the handoff before expanding it.
scenarios: A recurring renewal coordination support queue needs consistent attention while your manager focuses on decisions.
Several people contribute information, and the reviewer needs one current record with visible gaps.

faqs.question: What should we prepare for this role?
faqs.answer: Bring a current example, the approved source systems, the output you need, and the manager who can answer questions. Together we define what complete means and which situations must be escalated.

faqs.question: Can we begin with a limited scope?
faqs.answer: Yes. Start with one repeatable queue, review a sample of completed work, and improve the instructions before adding responsibilities.

faqs.question: Who handles exceptions or consequential decisions?
faqs.answer: Your authorized owner does. Support collects the context and records the question so the decision can be made by the right person, then follows the approved instruction.

research.title: Observing Health Signal Freshness in Account Reviews
research.description: A proposed observation protocol for recording whether each health signal used in an account review was current at the moment of decision, with source-specific age rules, a frozen evidence set, and a reproducible currency code. It defines a method and reports no completed study, no agreement rate, and no claim about any customer portfolio.

research.title: Evidence for QBR Action Closure
research.description: A proposed review protocol for quarterly business review actions that treats closure as a linked artifact plus customer acknowledgement rather than a status field. It specifies the observation unit, evidence classes, adverse cases, and reporting limits. No closure rate is measured here and no customer sample is claimed. The instrument is written for internal review of record quality, not for evaluating customer outcomes.

research.title: Reviewer Agreement on Onboarding Acceptance
research.description: A proposed agreement study for onboarding acceptance decisions. Two reviewers receive the same frozen milestone packet and independently rate each acceptance criterion before assigning accepted, conditionally accepted, or returned. The protocol reports no agreement statistic here, makes no claim about implementation quality, and does not assert that any customer accepted a milestone.

research.title: A Method for Dating Renewal Signals
research.description: A proposed method for dating renewal signals and measuring lead time from the first verified signal to a fixed renewal decision point. It defines signal classes, verification states, and the observation window, and reports no measured lead time for any portfolio. The method is a measurement design, not a forecast of renewal outcomes.

research.title: Coding Reliability in Customer Call Notes
research.description: A proposed reliability study for coding customer call notes. Notes are segmented into codeable units before any theme is assigned, then coded independently against a frozen codebook with field-level agreement reporting. No reliability coefficient is reported here and no coding exercise has been completed.
